name: 粋庵
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田淡路町2-105 ワテラスアネックス 0102
cuisine: A wa-modern Japanese restaurant on the Waterras Annex ground floor, opened April 2025: hon-maguro handled by a specialist, Ōmi beef bought from a dedicated supplier, and seasonal tempura, in courses at ¥8,000–¥9,999 for dinner against a ¥1,000–¥1,999 lunch, with a serious sake, shōchū and wine list. Twenty-eight seats, private rooms for two to six, and a ¥500 cover.
neighborhood: Kanda-Awajichō 2-chōme, in the Waterras Annex — 3 minutes from JR Ochanomizu (Chūō-Sōbu line), 3 minutes and 240 m from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), 3 minutes from Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line).
gf_detail: Nothing is published about allergens, and the shop's three headline items include one that is flatly out: the 天ぷら it advertises is wheat batter, fried in oil shared with everything else fried that service. The 本マグロ and 近江牛 sides of the menu are more negotiable in principle — but a wa-modern kaiseki kitchen seasons almost everything with wheat shōyu and mirin, and no gluten-free tamari is named. What this restaurant does have that most of the shard does not is the machinery for a conversation: it takes reservations, has private rooms, publishes an English menu, and is a 2025-opened room used for 接待 where dietary requests at booking are routine. Ask when you reserve, name the tempura and the soy sauce explicitly, and treat 'ask' as genuinely open here rather than as a polite no.
vegan_detail: Not advertised, but not obviously impossible. Tabelog records the kitchen as 野菜料理にこだわる as well as 魚料理にこだわる, and the format is a course built around seasonal ingredients, which is the format most able to substitute — but the named draws are tuna and Ōmi beef, and the dashi under a Japanese course is katsuo unless the kitchen is told otherwise. There is no published vegan course and no HappyCow-style listing. A vegan meal here would have to be arranged in advance, in Japanese or through the English menu contact, and confirmed as free of dashi and egg.

roles: 料理長 (head chef; not named on the restaurant's site)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Awajichō, Chiyoda-ku — the Waterras Annex, the retail podium of the Waterras redevelopment beside Ochanomizu
chef_bio.background: 粋庵 opened on 8 April 2025 on the ground floor of the Waterras Annex, the low-rise retail building of the Waterras complex between Ochanomizu and Awajichō. It presents itself as a 和モダン Japanese restaurant built for entertaining — 「接待やデートで使いたい和モダンな和食料理店」 — with three things at the centre of the menu: carefully selected hon-maguro, which the shop says is handled 「職人技でその魅力を最大限に引き出し」; Ōmi beef sourced from a dedicated specialist supplier; and tempura made from whatever is in season. Around that sits a drinks list the restaurant treats as equal billing, with sake, shōchū and wine all flagged by Tabelog as 「こだわる」. The room seats 28 across an eight-seat counter and twenty at tables, with private rooms for two, four and six, and can be taken over for parties up to fifty; there is a projector, power at the seats and free wi-fi, it is wheelchair-accessible, and there is an English menu and a children's menu. Payment is unusually open for a Japanese restaurant of this level — every major card including UnionPay, all the common electronic money, and PayPay, d払い, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay and Merpay — with a ¥500 charge per person and no service charge. Tabelog rates it 3.31, which mostly reflects how new it is.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「心ほどける、粋な味わいとともに」 — the shop's own line: carefully made Japanese food and warm hospitality in a calm room.
chef_bio.specialty: 本マグロ, 近江牛 and seasonal 天ぷら — the three items the restaurant names for itself — served in courses, with a sake and wine list treated as part of the offer.

anecdotes.text: The restaurant describes its own audience plainly: 「接待やデートで使いたい和モダンな和食料理店。厳選した本マグロ、近江牛、四季折々の食材を使った天ぷらを味わえる贅沢なコースが魅力です。」

It is unusually well equipped for a Japanese restaurant — projector, power sockets at the seats, free wi-fi, wheelchair access, an English menu and a children's menu — which is what a Waterras ground-floor unit built for corporate entertaining looks like.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13307697 lists 粋庵 under 新御茶ノ水/日本料理・海鮮・天ぷら at 東京都千代田区神田淡路町2-105 ワテラスアネックス0102, coordinates 35.69773/139.76815, 240 m and 3 minutes from Shin-Ochanomizu with JR Ochanomizu and Awajichō also 3 minutes away, tel 03-6206-4317 (booking line 050-5596-2821), an opening date of 2025年4月8日, 28 seats (8 counter, 20 table) with private rooms for 2/4/6 and hire up to 50, a ¥500 charge and no service charge, dinner budget ¥8,000–¥9,999 against ¥1,000–¥1,999 at lunch, weekday hours 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–22:00 with longer Saturday service and closure on Sundays and public holidays, an English menu, a children's menu, wheelchair access, free wi-fi, and 野菜料理にこだわる alongside 魚料理にこだわる. The restaurant's own site suian-japan.com confirms the identity and the ワテラス/御茶ノ水 location, gives the tagline 「心ほどける、粋な味わいとともに」, and describes the menu as 厳選した本マグロ, 近江牛 and seasonal tempura in course form. The official Instagram is @suian.japan.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Tempura is one of the three things the restaurant advertises, so wheat batter and a shared fryer are in the kitchen every service. No allergen information is published and no gluten-free preparation is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A 和モダン Japanese course kitchen with no tamari or gluten-free seasoning named anywhere; wheat shōyu and mirin should be assumed throughout.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The named centrepieces are hon-maguro and Ōmi beef, and the underlying dashi of a Japanese course is katsuo unless the kitchen is asked to change it.

positives.text: Reservations, private rooms and an English menu mean a dietary request can actually be made and understood in advance — the practical prerequisite for eating safely at a Japanese course restaurant.
Tabelog records the kitchen as 野菜料理にこだわる as well as 魚料理にこだわる, so vegetables are treated as more than garnish.

cultural_comfort.level: Among the easiest fine-ish Japanese rooms in the area
cultural_comfort.note: Ground floor of the Waterras Annex, three minutes from Ochanomizu, Shin-Ochanomizu and Awajichō alike — the light record's 「新御茶ノ水駅 (ワテラス)」 is exactly right. There is an English menu, free wi-fi, power at the seats, step-free access and a children's menu, and it takes almost every form of payment including UnionPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay, which makes it unusually low-friction for a visitor. Book: it has 28 seats and private rooms for two to six, and it is a room used for business entertaining, so walk-ins at dinner are a gamble. There is a ¥500 cover per person and no service charge. Closed Sundays and public holidays; Saturday runs a longer lunch (to 15:00) and an earlier dinner (16:00–21:00). Because it opened in April 2025 there is very little independent review coverage yet — the picture here comes from the restaurant's own copy and its Tabelog profile, so treat the food description as the house's claim rather than as a verdict.

enrich_note: Confirmed. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 粋庵 (HTTP 200, 128件) returns four restaurants with that exact name — in Nara, Shimane, Tokyo and (as 四季彩粋庵/珈琲専心粋庵 etc.) several compounds — and exactly one Tokyo 粋庵: 13307697 at 神田淡路町2-105 ワテラスアネックス, filed under 新御茶ノ水. That matches the light record on all three counts: the station, the ワテラス building named in the sweep's neighbourhood string, and the 日本料理・プレミアム genre. The restaurant's own site suian-japan.com independently confirms the Ochanomizu location and the wa-modern Japanese identity. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.697728, 139.768152), about 290 m from the sweep's approximate pin. Caveat for the reviewer: the shop opened on 8 April 2025 and its site is a Wix page whose menu content did not render to a scripted fetch, so prices here come from Tabelog's budget bands and the dish list from the restaurant's own meta description, not from a published お品書き. gf and vegan are both left at 'ask' — advertised tempura rules out a higher gluten tier, but the reservation, private-room and English-menu infrastructure make a pre-arranged meal genuinely plausible, which is why neither is set to 'no'.
